findings.finding: F1. Both branches of the spec's Change are closed: pmdoc/node.go:131-133 refuses a mark on any non-text node, so Go cannot read what the engine reads, and refusing by name would refuse `**a<b>**`, a document the editor itself holds (parse_test.go:122-124). Only the owner can accept what the reversal costs a reader.
findings.answer: D2: C1 moves the browser engine's reading, not Go's, and the plan records the departure and what it costs a reader (a comment and a past version stop drawing the mark; a linked image in a comment stops being a link). The architect's call is named in D2 with the one-line alternative (drop `image` from D1's list).

findings.finding: F2. The Summary's cause is unsupported — `**a<b>c**` holds no address and diverges the same way — and the real class is larger; dropUnstoredMarks already canonicalises image and hardbreak but not html or footnote_reference.
findings.answer: D1 takes the class as every inline leaf node (the four isInlineNodeType names other than text), measured at 155 corpus and 684 fuzz divergences; departure 2 records the corrected cause.

findings.finding: F3. A2 proves nothing about C1: differential.sh archives packages/envoy alone (:53) and builds engine.jsonl once from the working tree (:86), so the oracle moves with the change; `the url corpus shows 0 misreads` names no line the tool prints.
findings.answer: D8 states exactly that, keeps A2 as the no-Go-change proof (both `cmp`s exit 0 at T2's and T4's commits), and adds the two-engine measurement with per-corpus expected counts as the measurement that shows C1.

findings.finding: F4. A1's red run needs a procedure the spec does not state, `the siblings a fuzz around them finds` names no generator, and the fuzz finds shapes this design does not fix.
findings.answer: D5 spells the red run (a fork-point checkout with fixtures.json regenerated by main's engine, failing with `outside Proof schema: node "html" cannot have marks`); D6 commits gen/leaf-marks-corpus.ts; D12 and the findings section carve the two outside shapes out of A1 by name.

findings.finding: F5. A3 is vacuous under this design, or `rewritten` has no referent: the census compares Go's reading and bytes, and C1 changes no Go file.
findings.answer: D9 splits the census into a C2 column (Go's reading does change there, with the exact `<![A-Za-z]` candidate filter, and each latest version it finds is rewritten after the deploy) and a C1 column that is blast radius only; departure 3 records that the rewrite clause has no referent for C1.

findings.finding: F6. The engine has three parse seams and the past-version view goes through the one the first design missed: lib.ts:436-440 setMarkdown builds its own ParserState, and VersionView.tsx:94-110 calls it.
findings.answer: Measurement 7 names all three seams; D3 applies the rule at each; D6's unit test has one row per seam so a seam left out fails; T5's browser test reads the past version as its own surface.

findings.finding: F7. Two implementation traps: a JSON round trip or doc.check() throws for 3,568 of 38,101 because the image node declares title as a string and the parser sets null; and folding the strip into withBlockIds would discard it whenever no id was minted (block-ids.ts:232, block-ids.test.ts:107-108).
findings.answer: D3 forbids both by name and requires node.mark/node.copy, which the prototype used over all 38,101.

findings.finding: F8. The fix makes dropUnstoredMarks dead and removes the only counter watching LEGION-365.
findings.answer: D7 deletes them as a clean cutover, collapses diffTreeLinkingImages back into diffTree, and names the two prose sites that state the old rule.

findings.finding: F9. Sequencing and collisions with sjawhar/legion#2458 (open), #2481 (open) and dispatch://INFRA-722 (todo) over fixtures.json, wantNames, differential_test.go and packages/proof-editor/src.
findings.answer: D10 sets the base, the merge-on-conflict rule, `bun run gen` rather than a hand merge, alphabetical wantNames, and the Envoy message to the INFRA-722 architect that C1 moves that issue's D4 oracle.

findings.finding: F10. No acceptance criterion covers the only surface the change alters; the deployment rule requires a browser test red at the commit before and green at the head.
findings.answer: D8's reader table (measured on DOMSerializer under happy-dom) and T5's packages/dispatch/e2e/leaf-marks.e2e.ts, with its own acceptance row and T8's red run.

findings.answer: The Findings sent elsewhere section gives each a destination and a reason; D11 puts the one fragment in packages/envoy/.changes with `--custom Issue=pr<PR number>`.

specDepartures.spec: Change: "Go reads each such document as the engine does, or refuses it by name."
specDepartures.plan: For C1 (the five documents and their inline-leaf family) the browser engine's reading moves and Go does not change; C2 (the HTML declaration) follows the spec as written.
specDepartures.evidence: pmdoc/node.go:131-133 refuses a mark on any non-text node and FromJSON validates; a measured prosemirrorToYXmlFragment/yXmlFragmentToProsemirrorJSON round trip drops the mark from an html, image and hardbreak node every time; refusing instead would refuse `**a<b>**`, which parse_test.go:122-124 names as the thing not to do. Prototype: with the engine normalised, all 35,664 corpus documents Go reads are read identically by both, down from 155 divergences.

summary: The Summary's "Go's markdown reader … reads five corpus documents differently" stands, but the reader that changes is the browser engine's, in packages/proof-editor, not Go's.
outcome.scope: C1 touches packages/proof-editor/src (three parse seams), pmdoc's fixtures, corpus and differential harness, and packages/dispatch/e2e; no Go reader, renderer or refusal changes.

specDepartures.spec: Summary: the five documents hold "a web address followed by `<b>` and then emphasis delimiters, in the address reader sjawhar/legion#2373 added".
specDepartures.plan: The address reading is identical in both readers; the one difference is the mark the engine keeps on the inline leaf node. The class is every inline leaf node, not the address shapes.
specDepartures.evidence: `**a<b>c**`, which holds no address, diverges the same way. Over 38,101 corpus documents every Go-versus-engine reading difference is one cause: image 73, html 64, footnote_reference 18 (155). A 1,166-document fuzz adds hardbreak: 684 divergences.

summary: The cause is not the address reader of sjawhar/legion#2373; the five documents are 5 of 64 html cases of one class.
outcome.scope: A1's "the siblings a fuzz around them finds" is read as the inline-leaf class (four leaf kinds) plus C2's declaration class, not as address shapes.

specDepartures.spec: A3: "A census of every stored version is on the pull request, and each document it finds is rewritten."
specDepartures.plan: The census has two columns. C2's column can find stored versions whose reading changes, and each latest version it finds is rewritten after the deploy. C1's column is blast radius only: nothing is rewritten, because no Go file changes and the stored bytes are already right.
specDepartures.evidence: C1 changes no file under packages/envoy/internal/ other than tests, fixtures and corpus, so no stored version's Parse tree, refusal or rendering bytes can change; the proof is `cmp base.jsonl head.jsonl` at T2's and T4's commits. C2 changes Go's reading of `<!` plus a lower-case letter, so its candidate filter `<![A-Za-z]` is exact.

acceptance: A3's rewrite clause has no referent for C1; it is kept as written for C2.

specDepartures.spec: The "Also in scope" paragraph: "a comment holding the same line hides the declaration".
specDepartures.plan: A comment does not hide it: it draws the literal characters of the declaration in a span of its own. The difference a reader sees is the node kind and the stored bytes (`p \<!a> q` against `p <!a> q`).
specDepartures.evidence: Measured on DOMSerializer.fromSchema over the engine's reading under happy-dom: `p q` draws `p <!a> q`. markdown-engine.ts:210-213 says a body draws raw inline HTML as its literal characters. sjawhar/legion#2458's tester wrote "draws the declaration as raw HTML", which is what the measurement shows.

summary: A comment draws the declaration as the literal characters of a raw-HTML node; it does not hide it.
